briefings.title: From deepfakes to DNA: the science of watermarking AI
briefings.tldr: Google DeepMind's SynthID watermarking technology—developed over eight years for digital media like text, images, and video—has now expanded into biology as "SynthID Bio" to trace the provenance of AI-generated protein sequences and 3D structures without impacting their biological function.

briefings.title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

people.name: David Joseph
people.role: Chairman and CEO, Universal Music UK

briefings.tldr: Artificial Intelligence will be more profound than electricity or the internet and could transform human health and scientific discovery, but society must intentionally guide AI to enhance rather than replace human creativity and values.

briefings.title: Can AI help us better predict the weather?

people.name: Peter Battaglia
people.role: Senior Director of Research, Google DeepMind

briefings.tldr: AI models developed by Google DeepMind—such as GraphCast, GenCast, and WeatherNext 3—are revolutionizing global weather forecasting by bypassing traditional supercomputer fluid dynamics approximations in favor of learning statistical patterns directly from decades of historical meteorological data, achieving significant performance gains including early warnings for extreme events like Category 5 storms.

briefings.title: Understanding the inner thoughts of AI
briefings.tldr: Interpretability acts as the "neuroscience" of AI, reverse-engineering how neural networks learn to ensure safety and scientific understanding.

briefings.title: 10 years of AlphaGo: The turning point for AI | Thore Graepel & Pushmeet Kohli

people.name: Thore Graepel
people.role: AlphaGo team & Distinguished Research Scientist, Google DeepMind

briefings.tldr: The 2016 AlphaGo match against Lee Sedol marked the shift from AI as a tool for brute-force calculation to a system capable of creative intuition, establishing the reinforcement learning and search-space navigation techniques now used to solve grand scientific challenges like protein folding and mathematical proofs.
